architectural-decision-records.why: records the existing-enforcement guard decision and its limits
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR 0052: esk-genesis refuses a foreign gate-manifest.json by default and only reconciles against a manifest it generated; --adopt-existing takes one over non-destructively; provenance is a convenience check not authentication
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the guard ships discriminating tests that go red if it stops blocking
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added three tests: a foreign manifest is refused (exit 1, nothing deleted), --adopt-existing backs up and preserves foreign gates as repo-local, and our own manifest still reconciles (dropped gate removed); reverting the guard turns the refuse test red
quotes: replace each check with a no-op and require its test to fail

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the change adds executable logic, so the test level is explicit
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: fixture-driven tests run the real generator against a synthetic upstream and a planted foreign manifest; the right level for a file-writing generator, no integration surface beyond that
quotes: Fast, isolated tests for logic; a smaller number of integration tests for the seams

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: coupling fires on the added code; the behavior is committed as executable scenarios
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: implements refuse-by-default on a foreign manifest and consented non-destructive adoption, each pinned by a discriminating test
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment. Every time this

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: esk-genesis is the only writer/deleter in the system; the guard removes a destructive-write path
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: the guard prevents reconcile from deleting a consumer gate it did not install, keeps the existing path-containment (within/safeSkill) and manifest backup, and constrains takeover to an explicit flag
quotes: For the change in front of you, look up the matching sheet in the catalog below

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR states the limit rather than overclaiming
skeptical-audit.what: documented that provenance is inferred from manifest fields, not a signature, so it is a convenience check against accidental stomping and not an authentication boundary
quotes: content hash, a query, a version/commit SHA, or a URL + retrieval date;

judge-arch.why: reviewed in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context judge-arch review over the guard, the removals change, the tests, and the ADR: PASS 0 findings
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all

release-deployment-safety.why: a local generator guard; nothing deployed, migrated, or released

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: CI/dev tooling; no system, data, or resilience architecture change

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern selected; a provenance check plus a guard clause

sre-operational-readiness.why: no service, SLI/SLO, or alerting change

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal data, retention, or migration

arch-encode.why: a guard clause in a generator, not a rule encoded from a newly-caught mistake
